questions.question: What sets a PhD apart from other degrees?

options.A: Focus on practical skills and hands-on experience.
options.B: Development of critical thinking and analytical abilities.
options.C: Preparation to guide others in pursuing a PhD.
options.D: Completion of coursework and examinations.

questions.explanation: A PhD focuses on development of critical thinking and analytical abilities, and preparation to guide others in pursuing a PhD.

questions.question: What distinguishes a research-based degree from a typical undergraduate degree?

options.A: Clear and defined boundaries throughout the degree program.
options.B: Opportunities for continuous discovery and learning.
options.C: Graduation day marking the completion of the degree.
options.D: Acquisition of expertise and recognition in a specific field.

questions.explanation: A research-based degree offers opportunities for continuous discovery and learning, unlike the defined curriculum of an undergraduate degree.

questions.question: What is the importance of attitude and communication in the student-advisor relationship?

options.A: Having prior knowledge is the most important factor for a student to work towards a PhD.
options.B: Advisors expect students to define their own research problems without any guidance.
options.C: Students should choose advisors based on their reputation and availability.
options.D: Attitude, inclination to learn, and effective communication with the advisor are crucial.

questions.explanation: Attitude, inclination to learn, and effective communication with the advisor are crucial in the student-advisor relationship.

questions.question: What makes research challenging for first-time researchers?

options.A: The need to handle routine work and drudgery.
options.B: The sudden shift in patterns from coursework to research.
options.C: The discovery process involved in understanding the research process.
options.D: The pressure to obtain a degree and complete the research process.

questions.explanation: The sudden shift in patterns from coursework to research makes it challenging for first-time researchers.

questions.question: What is one advantage of research when dealing with failure?

options.A: Research allows for changing initial assumptions and exploring different approaches.
options.B: Research ensures that failures are minimized and success is guaranteed.
options.C: Research provides a predefined path to follow, for sure eliminating the possibility of failure.
options.D: Research discourages any changes in assumptions or approaches to maintain consistency.

questions.explanation: Research allows for changing initial assumptions and exploring different approaches when faced with failure.

questions.question: When conducting experiments and analysing results in research:

options.A: Each individual step will always lead to something significant.
options.B: The familiarity with the area helps in building experiments, but the results are often insignificant.
options.C: Day-to-day experiments and results are usually significant and groundbreaking.
options.D: Small steps are taken, and over time they contribute to something significant.

questions.explanation: Small steps are taken, and over time they contribute to something significant in research.

questions.question: Technologies in use today have life span of decades

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Technologies in use today do NOT have a lifespan of decades — they become obsolete in two to three years.

questions.question: Engineers aim to reduce the number of parts in a product

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Engineers aim to reduce the number of parts in a product to simplify manufacturing and reduce cost.

questions.question: Global warming is only a theoretical phenomenon

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Global warming is not merely theoretical — there is very strong experimental evidence that it is real.

questions.question: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere contributes to global warming

options.B: False

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere does contribute to global warming, and is the most significant contributor in terms of sheer quantity.

questions.question: Experimental data generated from a setup must validate the theoretical predictions or models designed for that setup

options.B: False
options.C: Sometimes
options.D: Never

questions.explanation: Experimental data only 'sometimes' validates theoretical predictions — the setup may have limitations.

questions.question: Literature survey is important because

options.A: It helps in getting a summary of work that has been done till date in some particular research area.
options.B: It is helpful in ensuring that a research work is not getting repeated.
options.C: It is helpful in understanding the approaches taken by scientists and what are the gaps in the processes.
options.D: It is helpful in clarifying the controversial results that one can get.

questions.explanation: Literature survey is important for all the listed reasons: getting a summary of existing work, ensuring research is not repeated, understanding gaps, and clarifying controversial results.

questions.question: Which of the following methods of searching for literature is suitable to identify the earliest contributor of a scientific outcome?

options.A: Keyword based search followed by sorting by year of publication
options.B: Citation based search followed by sorting by year of publication
options.C: Keyword based search followed by sorting by citations
options.D: Back reference based search following a keyword based search

questions.explanation: Back reference based search following a keyword based search is most suitable to identify the earliest contributor.

questions.question: Which of the following bibliographic details is a sufficient and unique piece of information to locate an article in an archival journal?

options.B: DOI
options.C: Page Number
options.D: Volume Number

questions.explanation: DOI (Digital Object Identifier) is a sufficient and unique piece of information to locate an article in an archival journal.

questions.question: Which of the following is always true for an open access journal?

options.A: Such journals are not peer reviewed
options.B: Articles in such a journal are freely available for download
options.C: Such journals charge for publication of an article
options.D: Such journals are of dubious reputation

questions.explanation: Articles in an open access journal are freely available for download — this is the defining characteristic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice to identify publications that need to be listed under references of an article?

options.B: Latest publications by the editor of the journal
options.C: Original publications in the topic of the article
options.D: Own publications referred in the article for further details

questions.explanation: Latest publications by the editor of the journal is NOT a recommended practice for identifying references.

questions.question: Which of the following indices is considered as a measure of the impact of a particular author in its area of his/her specialization?

options.B: Hirsch index of the author
options.C: Number of views of his/her latest article
options.D: Number of downloads of all articles in a year

questions.explanation: The Hirsch index (h-index) is considered as a measure of the impact of a particular author in their area of specialization.

questions.question: The following are categorized as primary source for literature survey

options.B: Conference proceedings & official publications
options.C: Compilations & reviews
options.D: Directories & year books

questions.explanation: Periodicals & research reports, and Conference proceedings & official publications are categorized as primary sources for literature survey.

questions.question: The abstracting databases for systematic manual searches include

options.B: PubMed
options.C: Wikipedia
options.D: Chemical Abstract (CA) service

questions.explanation: INSPEC and COMPENDEX, PubMed, and Chemical Abstract (CA) service are abstracting databases for systematic manual searches.

questions.question:
Consider that you have collected the following resources towards your research:
(1) A reference in a journal article that you have not referred yet
(2) A link to the website of a professional society
(3) A published article with journal, year, volume and page number
(4) An article from a newly launched journal with volume number, page number but year and ISSN number are due
(5) A newly accepted journal article with DOI link
(6) A book with an ISBN number available

Which of the following can be considered as archival (valuable record) references for inclusion in a publication?

options.B: Only 3, 5 and 6
options.C: Only 3, 4 and 6
options.D: Only 1, 2 and 5

questions.explanation: Only items 3 (published article with full bibliographic details), 5 (newly accepted journal article with DOI), and 6 (book with ISBN) can be considered as archival references.

weeks.title: Week 3: Data Analysis and Modelling Skills

questions.question: Safety must be the most important discipline of our routine when we are in laboratory or industrial environment. The common sources which have potential to cause damage, available in our lab towards which we need to be careful are-

options.B: Chemicals (Acids, Bases etc.)
options.C: Pressurized gas cylinders
options.D: Electricity and water source

questions.explanation: All options — sources of heat, chemicals, pressurized gas cylinders, and electricity/water sources — are common hazards in the lab.

questions.question: Which of the following statistics is used to quantify errors in parameter estimates?

options.B: Skewness
options.C: Standard deviation
options.D: Median

questions.explanation: Standard deviation is used to quantify errors in parameter estimates.

questions.question: A temperature sensor is installed at the bottom of the cooling tower storage tank to measure the temperature of outlet water. The sensor did not function properly for some time and gave data with higher temperature values. The conclusion we can draw from the process is-

options.A: Since data with different values were recorded, this increased the possibility of wide analysis thus very useful for our work
options.B: The data obtained cannot be reliable because these are not true data from the system but the malfunctioned one
options.C: The data can be used as with good accuracy using the predictive type data analysis where we can assume the extent of error and finally subtract the error from final value
options.D: None of these

questions.explanation: The data obtained cannot be reliable because these are not true data from the system but from the malfunctioned sensor.

questions.question: Which of the following can be treated as deterministic signals?

options.B: A sine wave corrupted by a rectangular pulse
options.C: Estimates of signals from measurements
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: A sine wave corrupted by a rectangular pulse can be treated as a deterministic signal as it follows a predictable pattern.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement(s) among the following w.r.t. non-linear models.

options.A: Linearization involves mere discarding of the non-linear terms in a model.
options.B: The standard Taylor's series-based linearized model changes with the nominal point of linearization.
options.C: A non-linear model can never yield a zero-valued output to a non-zero input.
options.D: Estimates of linear models have smaller errors than those of non-linear models.

questions.explanation: Statements A, C, and D are incorrect. Linearization is not mere discarding; a non-linear model can yield zero output; linear models do not always have smaller errors.

questions.question: Which of the following transforms are used to detect periodic (oscillatory) components in a signal?

options.B: z-transform
options.C: Fourier transform
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Fourier transform is used to detect periodic (oscillatory) components in a signal.

questions.question: The ratio of errors in parameter estimates of a model from two data sets with SNR 9 and 100 is
questions.explanation: The ratio of errors is 10:3 (since error is inversely proportional to SNR, ratio = √100 : √9 = 10 : 3).

questions.question: Which of the following is true concerning a parameter estimate?

options.A: It is in general close to the true value with high probability.
options.B: When averaged across a million experimental records under same operating conditions, the estimate equals the true value.
options.C: Least squares method always gives the estimate with lowest error.
options.D: It is a mathematical function of the observations.

questions.explanation: A parameter estimate is a mathematical function of the observations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Deterministic phenomena produce outcomes that can be predicted accurately.
options.B: Random processes occur randomly.
options.C: A process can produce a mix of deterministic and stochastic effects.
options.D: Signals that are random can never take negative values.

questions.explanation: Deterministic phenomena produce outcomes that can be predicted accurately, and a process can produce a mix of deterministic and stochastic effects.

questions.question: An estimator is said to be most efficient when

options.A: The parameters can be estimated in the least possible time.
options.B: The estimator provides accurate estimates with the smallest number of observations.
options.C: Standard error in the parameter estimates is lowest when compared to that of all other estimators.
options.D: It estimates parameters accurately even in presence of outliers.

questions.explanation: An estimator is most efficient when the standard error in the parameter estimates is lowest when compared to that of all other estimators.

questions.question: The title of a paper is 'Battery design and its impact'. This title

options.A: Identifies the area of research clearly
options.B: Indicates what is unique about the research
options.C: Does not identify the area of the research clearly
options.D: Does not indicate what is unique about the research

questions.explanation: The title 'Battery design and its impact' does not identify the area of research clearly and does not indicate what is unique about the research.

questions.question: In images

options.B: High magnification does not necessarily imply high resolution
options.C: Low magnification implies high resolution
options.D: High resolution implies low magnification

questions.explanation: High magnification does not necessarily imply high resolution in images.

questions.question: Tables are preferred over graphs

options.B: Never
options.C: Only when exact values need to be indicated
options.D: Only when trends in data need to be indicated

questions.explanation: Tables are preferred over graphs only when exact values need to be indicated.

questions.question: The length of a document

options.B: Indicates how little you know
options.C: Does not indicate anything about your knowledge
options.D: Does not indicate anything about the reader's knowledge

questions.explanation: The length of a document does not indicate anything about your knowledge or the reader's knowledge.

questions.question: The title of a paper should indicate the area of work as well as what is unique about the work.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: The title of a paper should indicate the area of work as well as what is unique about the work.

questions.question: In scientific documents sentences should be relatively short and to the point.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: In scientific documents, sentences should be relatively short and to the point for clarity.

questions.question: In an article, the image of a car engine must

options.A: Show the level of detail required for the discussion in the article
options.B: Have a marker bar indicating scale
options.C: Be in colour and not in black and white
options.D: Be in black and white and not in colour

questions.explanation: An image in an article must show the level of detail required for the discussion and have a marker bar indicating scale.

questions.question: Strategies one can use in the middle of a document include

options.B: Spatial strategy
options.C: Following a variable
options.D: Suspense strategy

questions.explanation: Chronological strategy, Spatial strategy, and Following a variable are strategies used in the middle of a document.

questions.question: While working with electricity only the voltage poses a danger to the users

options.B: False

questions.explanation: It is False — both voltage and current pose dangers to users when working with electricity.

questions.question: "Pouring rain results in clogged drains, and slippery roads. These clogged drains spill further water on to the roads." Use of the word 'these' in the previous sentence is ambiguous.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: The use of 'these' is not ambiguous — it clearly refers to 'clogged drains' mentioned in the previous clause.

questions.question: According to Sternberg's theories of intelligence practical intelligence relates to-

options.A: How one relates to the environment around them
options.B: How street smart they are
options.C: How well they come up with new theories
options.D: How well they solve new problems

questions.explanation: According to Sternberg, practical intelligence relates to how one relates to the environment around them and how street smart they are.

questions.question: Few research scholars collaborated to work on some specific area. They generated some data and analysed the results. Some of them published the result independently since they were the first to type it up. Is it ethical to do so?

options.A: Yes, because they have collaborated and know each other
options.B: No, all authors should know and agree with the publication
options.C: Yes, if the collaborators are junior to you
options.D: No, only if the authors are senior to you

questions.explanation: No, all authors should know and agree with the publication — publishing independently without co-authors' consent is unethical.

questions.question: Creativity is seen in

options.B: Science fiction
options.C: Engineering
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Creativity is seen in all areas — Drama, Science fiction, Engineering, and more.

questions.question: A good researcher is often well read in many areas

options.B: False

questions.explanation: True — a good researcher is often well read in many areas to draw connections across disciplines.

questions.question: We can work to the best of our potential when we are –

options.B: Eustressed
options.C: Hyper stressed
options.D: Distressed

questions.explanation: We can work to the best of our potential when we are Eustressed (positive, optimal stress level).

questions.question: The measure of a successful researcher is that the work of the researcher should be

options.A: Recognized by peers at an international level
options.B: Typically published in peer reviewed Journals
options.C: Mentioned in the campus magazine of the college
options.D: Must be discussed in the Department meeting of the researcher's department

questions.explanation: A successful researcher's work should be recognized by peers at an international level and typically published in peer reviewed journals.

questions.question: Creative people are

options.A: More likely to follow societal restrictions
options.B: Less likely to follow societal restrictions
options.C: More likely to think within the limits of previous work in the area
options.D: More likely to come up with a surprisingly new solution to a problem

questions.explanation: Creative people are less likely to follow societal restrictions and more likely to come up with surprisingly new solutions to problems.

questions.question: A PhD usually makes you

options.A: A specialist in one narrow area
options.B: A person who conducts experiments fast
options.C: A person who has a wide knowledge in a wide range of topics
options.D: A person who makes excellent sketches

questions.explanation: A PhD usually makes you a specialist in one narrow area.

questions.question: To become a good researcher, one must usually

options.B: Have mastery over specific techniques
options.C: Have a line of investigation
options.D: Be aware of recent advances in the field

questions.explanation: To become a good researcher, one must have good communication skills, mastery over specific techniques, a line of investigation, and be aware of recent advances.

questions.question: The followings can be attributed to a fully professional researcher-

options.A: They have some fundamental concepts that their peers (international) might be interested in
options.B: They have command over their area
options.C: They are aware of the situation where they can make significant contribution
options.D: They work without focusing on literature in the area

questions.explanation: A fully professional researcher has fundamental concepts, command over their area, and awareness of where they can make significant contributions.

questions.question: Which of the following falls in the category of intellectual property?

options.A: An original set of ideas or research results
options.B: Ideas originating from real property
options.C: Properties emanating from human creative labor
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Intellectual property includes original sets of ideas or research results, and properties emanating from human creative labor.

questions.question: Violations of Intellectual Property Rights leads to

options.B: Casual penalties
options.C: No big deal as we have license of fundamental rights to do whatever we want
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: Violations of Intellectual Property Rights lead to Infringement and Casual penalties.

questions.question: In order to obtain legal protection, you don't have to register which of the following types of intellectual property rights?

options.B: Patents
options.C: Designs
options.D: Geographical Indications

questions.explanation: Copyrights are automatically granted and do not require registration to obtain legal protection.

questions.question: A person invents a new process to capture musical performance on tape, he/she will most likely apply for–

options.B: Trade Marks
options.C: Patents
options.D: Trade Secret

questions.explanation: A new process or invention is protected by Patents.

questions.question: Use of an unregistered trade mark of a competitor shall amount to a tort of–

options.B: Fraud
options.C: Negligence
options.D: Passing off

questions.explanation: Use of an unregistered trade mark of a competitor amounts to the tort of 'Passing off'.

questions.question: What does an IP right entitle a person?

options.A: Right to file a suit in case of an infringement
options.B: Right of excludability
options.C: Right of commercial exploitation
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: An IP right entitles a person to all three: right to file a suit, right of excludability, and right of commercial exploitation.

questions.question: The Reebok Delta symbol and Hyundai Logo are protected by–

options.B: Trade Marks
options.C: Trade dress
options.D: Geographical Indications

questions.explanation: Brand logos and symbols like Reebok Delta and Hyundai Logo are protected by Trade Marks.

questions.question: Under the Patents Act, 1970, the person entitled to receive a patent on a new invention is–

options.A: The one who invented the invention first
options.B: The one who commercialise the invention first
options.C: The one who thought of the invention first
options.D: The one who filed a patent application first

questions.explanation: Under the Patents Act, 1970, the person who filed a patent application first is entitled to receive the patent.

questions.question: What is the term of a Patent in India?

options.B: 25 years
options.C: 10 years
options.D: 15 years

questions.explanation: The term of a patent in India is 20 years from the date of filing.

questions.question: What is the full form of TRIPS?

options.A: Tariff Related Aspects of Intellectual Properties
options.B: Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Science
options.C: The Registration of Intellectual Property
options.D: Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights

questions.explanation: TRIPS stands for Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.

questions.question: In the true experimental research design:

options.B: Less control on external variables
options.C: Control on external variables by randomization
options.D: No use of randomization

questions.explanation: In the true experimental research design, there is control on external variables by randomization.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incomplete experimental research design?

options.A: Before and after with control group design
options.B: Factorial design
options.C: One group before-after design
options.D: Latin Square design

questions.explanation: One group before-after design is an incomplete experimental research design as it lacks a control group.

questions.question: Coefficient of Determination is said to be unity when -

options.A: Error Sum of Squares is zero
options.B: Total Sum of Squares is zero
options.C: Regression Sum of Squares is zero
options.D: Regression Sum of Squares is same as Total Sum of Squares

questions.explanation: Coefficient of Determination (R²) is unity when Error Sum of Squares is zero and Regression Sum of Squares is same as Total Sum of Squares.

questions.question: The probability density function describes the following -

options.A: Probability of a phenomenon occurring in macro scale
options.B: Probability of a phenomenon occurring in micro scale
options.C: Distribution of probabilities in the continuous random variable domain
options.D: Distribution of probabilities in some particular set of undefined variables

questions.explanation: The probability density function describes the distribution of probabilities in the continuous random variable domain.

questions.question: During Response Surface Methodology's Canonical Analysis involving two factors, maximum response is said to be achieved when the eigen values of the B matrix are

options.B: all negative
options.C: all zero
options.D: such that one is positive and the other is negative

questions.explanation: Maximum response is achieved when all eigen values of the B matrix are negative (indicating a maximum point).

questions.question: Experiments are conducted in laboratories to

options.B: Obtain trends when theory is not known
options.C: Find effect of different variables on the desired response
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Experiments are conducted in laboratories for all the listed reasons.

questions.question: SPC and Design of Experiments are very closely interrelated.

options.B: False

questions.explanation: True — Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments are indeed closely interrelated.

questions.question: Which of these is not an application of experimental design in the field of Engineering design?

options.A: Evaluation and comparison of basic design configurations
options.B: Evaluation of material alternatives
options.C: Evaluation of key product design parameters that impact performance
options.D: Evaluation of correct process to develop the product

questions.explanation: Evaluation of correct process to develop the product is not an application of experimental design in Engineering design.

questions.question: The average estimated from a data collection is 50 cm. The quantity (quantities) which has the same units as the data is (are)

options.B: Median
options.C: Mode
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Standard deviation, Median, and Mode all have the same units as the data.

questions.question: Sample collected from an instrument giving binary data has the following values {1, -1, -1, 1, 1, -1} Mean of the above data set is
In order to pursue the research, which of the following is priorly required?

options.B: Formulating a research question
options.C: Deciding about the data analysis procedure
options.D: Formulating a research hypothesis

questions.explanation: Formulating a research question is the first step required to pursue research.

questions.question: Which one among the following statements is false in the context of participatory research?

options.B: It is a collective process of inquiry
options.C: It emphasizes people as experts
options.D: Its sole purpose is the production of knowledge

questions.explanation: Its sole purpose is NOT the production of knowledge — participatory research also emphasizes empowerment and social change.

questions.question: How to judge the depth of any research?

options.B: By research duration
options.C: By research objectives
options.D: By total expenditure on research

questions.explanation: The depth of research is judged by research objectives.

questions.question: What is the main aim of Interdisciplinary research?

options.A: To over simplify the problem of research
options.B: Integrating knowledge from multiple disciplines to solve a problem.
options.C: To create a new trend in research methodology
options.D: To reduce the emphasis on a single subject in the research domain

questions.explanation: The main aim of interdisciplinary research is integrating knowledge from multiple disciplines to solve a problem.

questions.question: Electron microscopes can be used in reverse to write in extremely small areas

options.B: False

questions.explanation: True — electron beam lithography uses electron microscopes in reverse to write in extremely small areas.

questions.question: What are the core elements of a dissertation?

options.A: Introduction; Data Collection; Data Analysis; Conclusions and Recommendations
options.B: Executive Summary; Literature Review; Data Gathered; Conclusions; Bibliography
options.C: Research Plan; Research Data; Analysis; References
options.D: Introduction; Literature Review; Research Methodology; Results; Discussions and Conclusions

questions.explanation: The core elements of a dissertation are: Introduction; Literature Review; Research Methodology; Results; Discussions and Conclusions.

questions.question: How can we enhance the research objective?

options.B: By making it more reliable
options.C: By making it more impartial
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Research objectives can be enhanced by making them more valid, reliable, and impartial.

questions.question: A common test in research demands much priority on

options.B: Useability
options.C: Objectivity
options.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: A common test in research demands priority on reliability, useability, and objectivity — all of the above.

questions.question: An appropriate source to find out descriptive information is

options.B: Directory
options.C: Encyclopedia
options.D: Dictionary

questions.explanation: An encyclopedia is an appropriate source to find out descriptive information.

questions.question: Mahabalipuram in south-east India, pre-eminently testimony to the ________ civilization

options.B: Mauryas
options.C: Guptas
options.D: Cholas

questions.explanation: Mahabalipuram in south-east India is pre-eminently testimony to the Pallavas civilization.

weeks.title: Week 9: The Research Journey
weeks.topic: Research Journey, Navigating Uncertainty, Setbacks, and Discovery

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics distinguish a research programme from a regular curriculum-oriented academic programme?

options.A: The research question may itself require extensive exploration before becoming well defined.
options.B: Experimental outcomes may deviate from expectations and require modification of the research approach.
options.C: The programme follows a highly predictable schedule with predefined learning outcomes for every stage.
options.D: The researcher may repeatedly formulate new questions as insights emerge from previous work.

questions.explanation: Research programmes are distinguished by open-ended questions, unexpected experimental outcomes, and iterative question formulation — unlike fixed academic curricula.

questions.question: The lecture compares the research journey to a roller-coaster ride primarily because:

options.A: Research requires researchers to work continuously under high pressure.
options.B: Research consists of predictable stages followed by unavoidable examinations.
options.C: Research involves alternating periods of progress, uncertainty, setbacks, breakthroughs, and renewed progress.
options.D: Research is primarily dependent on collaboration with a large number of researchers.

questions.explanation: The research journey is compared to a roller-coaster ride because it involves alternating periods of progress, uncertainty, setbacks, breakthroughs, and renewed progress.

questions.question: According to the lecture, which factors can contribute to the overall research experience of a scholar in a laboratory?

options.B: Emotional experiences and friendships
options.C: Availability and accessibility of research facilities
options.D: Support received from friends and family

questions.explanation: All listed factors — relationships with advisers, emotional experiences, research facilities, and external support — contribute to the overall research experience.

questions.question: Which practices are presented in the lecture as useful for maintaining a sustainable rhythm in research life?

options.B: Taking time for recreation and renewal
options.C: Reflecting periodically on one's activities and decisions
options.D: Working continuously for extremely long hours whenever a problem arises

questions.explanation: Adequate sleep, recreation, and periodic reflection are practices for maintaining a sustainable rhythm in research life.

questions.question: A researcher receives harsh feedback from an adviser and immediately feels angry and personally inadequate. Based on the lecture, what should be the most appropriate immediate response?

options.A: Respond immediately to the adviser to defend the research.
options.B: Suppress the emotion completely and continue working without reflection.
options.C: Pause, recognize the emotion, regulate it through techniques such as rhythmic breathing, and then respond with greater clarity.
options.D: Discuss the adviser's behaviour with all labmates immediately.

questions.explanation: The appropriate response is to pause, recognize the emotion, regulate it through techniques such as rhythmic breathing, and then respond with greater clarity.

questions.question: Which of the following strategies are specifically discussed in the lecture as ways of processing or reducing intense anger?

options.B: Temporarily stepping away from the situation
options.C: Journaling what one is feeling
options.D: Immediately confronting the person responsible for the trigger

questions.explanation: Rhythmic breathing, stepping away, and journaling are strategies discussed for processing intense anger.

questions.question: A research scholar feels discouraged after a labmate's paper is accepted while their own paper remains unpublished. Which response best reflects the approach advocated in the lecture?

options.A: Compare the two researchers and conclude that the labmate is more capable.
options.B: Suppress the feeling of comparison without examining its cause.
options.C: Convert the comparison into curiosity by investigating what the labmate did differently and identifying possible improvements in one's own approach.
options.D: Avoid interacting with the labmate until one's own paper is accepted.

questions.explanation: The lecture advocates converting comparison into curiosity by investigating what the labmate did differently and identifying improvements.

questions.question: According to the lecture, prolonged emotional distress or isolation can negatively affect which aspects of a researcher's life?

options.B: Only the researcher's publication record
options.C: Physical health
options.D: Friendships and social relationships

questions.explanation: Prolonged emotional distress can negatively affect research progress, physical health, and friendships and social relationships.

questions.question: A researcher becomes stuck on a difficult problem and begins working for very long hours while withdrawing from friends and labmates. According to the lecture, what is the primary concern with this response?

options.A: It demonstrates insufficient commitment to independent research.
options.B: Emotional isolation may worsen the situation and negatively affect research progress as well as personal well-being.
options.C: Long working hours always produce incorrect experimental results.
options.D: Researchers should never attempt to solve difficult problems independently.

questions.explanation: The primary concern is that emotional isolation may worsen the situation and negatively affect both research progress and personal well-being.

questions.question: Which of the following constitute potential support systems for a research scholar according to the lecture?

options.B: Labmates and friends
options.C: Mentor
options.D: Family or old friends

questions.explanation: All listed groups — adviser/supervisor, labmates, mentor, and family/old friends — constitute potential support systems for a research scholar.

questions.question: Students in schools typically expect

options.B: Question paper patterns to be finalized in advance
options.C: Clarity on the 'portions' for an exam
options.D: Questions outside the syllabus

questions.explanation: Students in schools typically expect well defined questions, question paper patterns finalized in advance, and clarity on the 'portions' for an exam.

questions.question: From the perspective of a school student the question 'How long will it take to go from Chennai to Kolkata' is

options.B: Is a well defined question
options.C: Is typically how a full question is framed in an exam
options.D: Has a unique

questions.explanation: From a school student's perspective, this is a 'poorly' defined question as it lacks specifics about mode of transport, route, etc.

questions.question: The format of exams in schools

options.B: Teaches you to breakdown a problem to parts and solve them
options.C: Prepares you for a professional setting
options.D: Teaches you to handle unexpected questions

questions.explanation: School exam formats help understand fundamentals, teach problem breakdown, and prepare for professional settings.

questions.question: A typical professional workplace requires you to

options.B: Solve 'poorly' defined problems
options.C: Focus on syllabus
options.D: Work within a question paper pattern

questions.explanation: A typical professional workplace requires you to handle open ended questions and solve 'poorly' defined problems.

questions.question: Learning in college is expected to

options.B: Focus only on well-defined problems
options.C: Teach you to handle open ended problems
options.D: Follow the same approach used in school

questions.explanation: Learning in college is expected to prepare you for professional life and teach you to handle open ended problems.

questions.question: Applying a known theory to one additional new situation is most likely

options.B: Incremental research
options.C: Transformational research
options.D: Important contribution to research

questions.explanation: Applying a known theory to one additional new situation is most likely incremental research.

questions.question: Use of a series of Experimental techniques to study the same phenomenon across different samples is typically an example of:

options.B: Transformational research
options.C: Incremental research
options.D: Breakthrough research

questions.explanation: Using a series of experimental techniques to study the same phenomenon across different samples is typically systematic research.

questions.question: In the development of phones, which of the following can be considered transformational

options.B: First deployment of the cordless phone
options.C: The improvement from cordless phone to mobile phone
options.D: Making the first-generation mobile phones smaller and more colorful

questions.explanation: The improvement from cordless phone to mobile phone is transformational as it fundamentally changed how phones are used.

questions.question: In the development of bicycles, which of the following can be considered transformational

options.A: Improvement from wooden seat to cushioned seat
options.B: Making the seat more ergonomic
options.C: Adding a carrier
options.D: Adding gears to a bicycle

questions.explanation: Adding gears to a bicycle is transformational as it fundamentally changed the capability and usage of bicycles.

questions.question: In the development of airplanes, we can associate imagination with

options.A: Designing fixed wings even though birds have flapping wings
options.B: Adding seats inside an airplane
options.C: Creating a cargo version of the airplane
options.D: Adding more engines to the airplane

questions.explanation: Designing fixed wings even though birds have flapping wings represents imagination — breaking free from direct imitation of nature.

weeks.title: Week 11: Role of AI in Research
weeks.topic: Role of AI in Research & Generative AI

questions.question: Consider the example of a machine learning program that learned to play checkers. Which of the following statements are correct?

options.A: The machine was explicitly programmed with every possible checkers strategy.
options.B: The machine learned through experience by repeatedly playing the game.
options.C: The example is associated with an early instance of reinforcement learning.
options.D: The example demonstrates that AI-based learning is a phenomenon that began only with generative AI.

questions.explanation: The machine learned through experience by repeatedly playing the game, and this is an early instance of reinforcement learning.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly reflect the lecture's discussion of classical AI and generative AI?

options.A: Generative AI is the only appropriate approach for solving modern research problems.
options.B: Classical AI methods can still provide effective solutions for domain-specific problems.
options.C: Researchers should select an AI approach according to the problem rather than assuming that generative AI must always be used.
options.D: Classical AI became irrelevant after the emergence of LLMs.

questions.explanation: Classical AI can still be effective for domain-specific problems, and researchers should select AI approaches based on the problem.

questions.question: Consider an LLM that predicts the next token from the context provided to it. Which of the following statements are correct?

options.A: The probability of a token can depend on the preceding context.
options.B: A token with the highest probability must always be generated.
options.C: Different contexts can result in different probability distributions for the next token.
options.D: The model can repeatedly predict tokens to construct a longer response.

questions.explanation: Token probability depends on context, different contexts give different distributions, and the model builds responses by repeatedly predicting tokens.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguish token size, context size, and parameter count in an LLM?

options.A: Token size is related to the vocabulary of words or subwords that the model can generate.
options.B: Context size refers to the amount of previous token information considered by the model.
options.C: Parameter count refers to the number of tokens that can be stored in the prompt.
options.D: Parameter count is related to how the learned probability distributions are represented in the model.

questions.explanation: Token size relates to vocabulary, context size to previous token information, and parameter count to learned probability distributions.

questions.question: Which statements correctly describe the role of vector representations in the LLM framework explained in the lecture?

options.A: A very large probability matrix can be represented through a comparatively smaller-dimensional vector space.
options.B: Different contexts may be projected to nearby locations in the vector space.
options.C: Such compression can contribute to variability and errors because information from different contexts may influence generation.
options.D: Every possible context is retained as a completely independent point with no overlap.

questions.explanation: Vector representations allow compression of large probability matrices, project similar contexts nearby, and can contribute to variability/errors.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are consistent with the lecture's explanation of alignment?

options.A: Alignment can modify model behaviour so that generated probabilities better correspond to desired outcomes.
options.B: Alignment may be directed towards objectives such as factuality, bias reduction or local context.
options.C: Alignment guarantees that all outputs produced by an LLM are factually correct.
options.D: Reinforcement learning from human preferences is associated with the alignment process.

questions.explanation: Alignment modifies model behaviour, can target factuality/bias, and uses reinforcement learning from human preferences — but does not guarantee factual correctness.

questions.question: A researcher asks a small language model a question whose meaning is ambiguous. Relevant information is retrieved from an internal repository and added to the original question before generating the answer. Which statements correctly describe this approach?

options.A: The approach is consistent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
options.B: The retrieved information provides additional context to the model.
options.C: The approach necessarily requires retraining the entire language model.
options.D: Additional context can make the model's response more focused.

questions.explanation: This is RAG — retrieved information adds context and can focus responses, without requiring model retraining.

questions.question: The lecture uses the example of the 2011 ICC World Cup to explain the effect of retrieval-augmented generation. Which of the following correctly captures the idea?

options.A: Additional retrieved information can contextualize an otherwise ambiguous query.
options.B: The original question can be effectively shifted toward a more appropriate contextual representation.
options.C: RAG works primarily by increasing the number of parameters in the LLM.
options.D: A richer context can increase the probability of producing the intended

questions.explanation: RAG contextualizes ambiguous queries, shifts contextual representation, and increases probability of intended output — not by increasing parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about hallucination are correct according to the lecture?

options.A: A model may produce a plausible answer even when the generated information does not match the ground truth.
options.B: Hallucination can occur when the model has insufficiently represented information or context.
options.C: Hallucination can be reduced through techniques such as providing larger context, but it cannot necessarily be eliminated completely.
options.D: Hallucination means that the model has deliberately decided to provide false information.

questions.explanation: Hallucination can produce plausible but false answers, occurs due to insufficient context, and can be reduced but not eliminated — it is not deliberate.

questions.question: A language model produces a misleading recommendation because a false or deliberately misleading article was present in information from which the model learned. Which statements are appropriate?

options.A: The problem is necessarily an example of hallucination.
options.B: AI systems can potentially propagate misinformation present in their information sources.
options.C: A response may be misleading even when it is not simply an invented fact by the model.
options.D: Independent verification of important AI-generated information remains necessary.

questions.explanation: AI can propagate misinformation from sources, responses can be misleading without hallucination, and independent verification is necessary.

weeks.title: Week 12: Hypothesis Generation and Metacognition
weeks.topic: Hypothesis Generation, Thinking Habits & Metacognition in Research

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguish course-based education from research-based education as discussed in the lecture?

options.A: Course-based education primarily deals with an existing body of knowledge, whereas PhD research is expected to create new knowledge.
options.B: A PhD programme follows a common prescribed syllabus and curriculum in the same way as a course-based degree.
options.C: Course-based education generally has a prescribed syllabus and curriculum, whereas research-based education does not simply follow a fixed syllabus.
options.D: Knowledge acquired in course-based education and new knowledge generated through PhD research are evaluated in exactly the same way.

questions.explanation: Course-based education deals with existing knowledge with a prescribed syllabus, while PhD research creates new knowledge without a fixed syllabus.

questions.question: A research scholar is beginning a PhD and expects the research guide to provide a complete step-by-step procedure for the entire research programme. Which responses are consistent with the lecture?

options.A: The scholar should recognize that PhD research involves substantially self-directed work.
options.B: The absence of a fixed syllabus means that the scholar does not need guidance from the research guide.
options.C: The research guide can provide guidance and support when ambiguity or difficulty arises.
options.D: The scholar is expected to develop the ability to decide how the research should progress.

questions.explanation: PhD research is self-directed, the guide provides support when needed, and the scholar must develop the ability to direct their own research.

questions.question: A researcher proposes a hypothesis based on existing knowledge and experience. Which conditions, according to the lecture, are relevant to treating it as a scientific hypothesis?

options.A: It should be an educated prediction rather than a statement already established as true.
options.B: It should allow a possibility of being disproved.
options.C: It should be protected from contradictory observations by adding explanations that cannot be tested.
options.D: Its truth must be established before experiments or data collection begin.

questions.explanation: A scientific hypothesis should be an educated prediction and must allow a possibility of being disproved (falsifiability).

questions.question: Consider the hypothesis: 'All swans are white.' Based on the falsifiability example in the lecture, which statements are correct?

options.A: Finding a black swan would provide an observation capable of disproving the hypothesis.
options.B: It is necessary to observe every swan in the world before the hypothesis can be scientifically examined.
options.C: The possibility of disproving the hypothesis is central to the criterion discussed in the lecture.
options.D: The criterion discussed emphasizes the possibility of disproof rather than establishing the hypothesis as permanently true.

questions.explanation: A black swan disproves the hypothesis; falsifiability (possibility of disproof) is central, not permanent truth establishment.

questions.question: A student starts a PhD after being given a broad research topic. According to the lecture, which actions are appropriate before arriving at a testable hypothesis?

options.A: Begin by formulating relevant questions about the topic and considering why the topic is important.
options.B: Start an unrestricted literature survey immediately and use it as the only route for identifying the research problem.
options.C: Use literature exploration and observations to refine the initial questions through repeated cycles.
options.D: Formulate the final testable hypothesis immediately from the broad topic without further exploration.

questions.explanation: Begin with relevant questions and use literature exploration and observations to iteratively refine the questions before arriving at a testable hypothesis.

questions.question: In the obesity and eating-habit example, observations from the literature and study were used to identify an anomaly and develop a hypothesis. Which statements are supported by the lecture?

options.A: An anomaly can arise when observations do not match a commonly assumed explanation.
options.B: The observed influence of factors such as the amount of food offered can motivate further investigation.
options.C: The hypothesis was formulated directly from the broad topic without literature survey or observations.
options.D: Identifying a missing link or contradiction can provide scope for further research and help generate a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: Anomalies arise from mismatches, observed factors motivate investigation, and identifying contradictions helps generate hypotheses.

questions.question: According to the Revised Bloom's Taxonomy discussed in the lecture, which statements are correct?

options.A: Remember, Understand and Apply are described as lower-order thinking levels.
options.B: Analyze, Evaluate and Create are described as higher-order thinking levels.
options.C: Create is placed below Remember because generating a new idea generally requires less cognitive effort.
options.D: The taxonomy states that every individual experiences exactly the same difficulty across all six levels.

questions.explanation: Remember/Understand/Apply are lower-order and Analyze/Evaluate/Create are higher-order thinking levels in Revised Bloom's Taxonomy.

questions.question: A PhD scholar collects experimental data, examines unfamiliar patterns, considers alternative hypotheses, and develops a new research idea. Which Bloom's levels are most directly represented by these activities?

options.B: Evaluate
options.C: Remember
options.D: Create

questions.explanation: Examining patterns (Analyze), considering alternatives (Evaluate), and developing new ideas (Create) are represented by these activities.

questions.question: Which statements correctly reflect the lecture's discussion of the role of higher-order thinking in PhD research?

options.A: All six levels of thinking may be used during research problem solving.
options.B: The lecture identifies analysis as an important starting level in PhD research because researchers collect and analyze data.
options.C: The main intellectual focus of a PhD is memorizing information from the existing body of knowledge.
options.D: Evaluation can involve considering alternate hypotheses and attempting to validate them.

questions.explanation: All thinking levels may be used, analysis is an important starting level, and evaluation involves considering alternate hypotheses.

questions.question: Which statements are consistent with the lecture's discussion of creativity and functional fixedness?

options.A: Creative thinking can be developed or improved through practice rather than being limited to an ability fixed at birth.
options.B: Functional fixedness can cause a person to perceive an object only through its conventional purpose and can hinder lateral thinking.
options.C: Complete knowledge of the existing body of knowledge guarantees the creation of something new.
options.D: Functional fixedness helps researchers generate new approaches when facing unexpected or novel challenges.

questions.explanation: Creative thinking can be developed through practice, and functional fixedness limits perception to conventional purposes, hindering lateral thinking.
